title: Zero Cold Starts: Serverless AI Agents on Akamai Functions — Thorsten Hans
talk_summary: Thorsten Hans demos building MCP servers and AI agents as WebAssembly components with the CNCF Spin framework, deployed to Akamai Functions for globally distributed, zero-cold-start execution. The talk is mostly a vendor/product demo of Spin, wmcp, and Akamai Functions rather than a study of agent orchestration or model economics.

takeaways.technique: Compose MCP servers from off-the-shelf components instead of hand-rolling protocol/auth
takeaways.what_they_do: Use the wmcp CLI to scaffold only tool/resource/prompt business logic, then compose a full MCP server where auth (OAuth2/OIDC) and protocol handling are provided by reusable components.
takeaways.evidence_quote: everything else all those non-functional requirements that we have to tackle right like for example authenticating users using of 2 and OIDC that's done by WMCP

takeaways.technique: WASM components as tiny portable deploy units
takeaways.what_they_do: Compile agent/MCP code to WebAssembly components that are small, sandboxed, and portable across WASI-compliant runtimes, with permissions explicitly granted.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they are binaries super tiny in size, easy to distribute, super fast to run and portable

takeaways.technique: Snapshot-based warm start for interpreted runtimes
takeaways.what_they_do: At compile time, load the JS interpreter and dependencies, evaluate global scope, then snapshot memory to disk so each request starts from a pre-warmed state.
takeaways.numbers: cold start <0.5 ms claimed; full LLM loop ~820-866 ms

takeaways.technique: Single-command deploy with built-in KV store
takeaways.what_they_do: One deploy command distributes the workload to ~60 regions, each health-checked before DNS rollout; a multi-tenant key-value store is auto-provisioned per app.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we are globally distributed in roughly 60 seconds
